\section{Dissolved Oxygen Regime}
Dawn minima of dissolved oxygen were logged in all twelve ponds
of the intensive block over the full grow-out cycle.
The saturation concentration \Csat\ at the morning temperature
sets the ceiling for overnight recovery,
and ponds rarely returned to more than 85\% of \Csat\ before sunrise.
Aerators were scheduled from 02:00 to 06:00 in \pond{7} and \pond{9},
where the drop was fastest after feeding days.

Afternoon supersaturation above 120\% of \Csat\ was common
in the shallow nursery units,
a sign of dense phytoplankton blooms that then crashed at night.
The bloom--crash cycle explains most of the dawn stress events
recorded by the loggers.

Unionised ammonia \amm\ stayed below the 0.05~mg/L guideline
in every pond except the two nursery units,
where feeding density was highest.
The guideline was exceeded only after the June pump failure,
and recovery took three days of doubled water exchange.

\section{Feeding Protocol}
A probiotic dose of \dose{0.5} was applied weekly to each grow-out pond
as a water-borne treatment after the morning exchange.
During the finfish trial the dose was raised to \dose{1.2}
for the first four weeks, then tapered to the standard level.

Feed conversion stayed near $\fcr = 1.4$ across the cycle
for the shrimp ponds on the standard ration.
The trial ration pushed $\fcr$ down to 1.25 in \pond{4},
but the margin did not cover the ration cost at current prices.

Daily ration was set at 3\% of estimated biomass per \ha,
adjusted weekly against the cast-net samples.
Feeding was suspended whenever the dawn oxygen reading
fell below 3~mg/L, and resumed at half ration for a day.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Block & Ration (kg/day) & Observed $\fcr$ \\
\midrule
Grow-out north & 41 & 1.42 \\
Grow-out south & 38 & 1.39 \\
Nursery & 9 & 1.18 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Mean daily ration and feed conversion by block.}
\end{table}

The nursery block converted feed best,
as expected from the higher temperature and smaller animals.

\section{Stocking and Harvest Notes}
Post-larvae were stocked at 45 per square metre in the grow-out block
after a ten-day acclimation in the nursery units.
Salinity was held near 18~ppt through the cycle,
and \Csat\ was re-estimated whenever the morning temperature
shifted by more than two degrees.

Survival to harvest averaged 78\% across the block,
with the lowest value in \pond{11} after the June pump failure.
Ammonia \amm\ spiked there for three days
before the exchange rate was doubled.

Harvest was done by drain netting over two mornings per pond,
and the animals were iced on the bank within twenty minutes.
Mean harvest size was 21~g on the standard ration
and 23~g on the trial ration.

The next cycle will trial a lower density in the two nursery units
and a staggered harvest to smooth the cash flow.
A second aerator is budgeted for \pond{11} before restocking.
